premises: Local differences in atomic vibrational amplitudes exist in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles due to dissimilar bonding strengths and atomic masses.
These vibrational differences drive heterogeneous premelting by initiating localized disorder before complete melting.
MD simulations can quantify these local vibrational amplitudes and atomic displacement distributions.
The predicted outcome is localized regions of increased vibrational disorder observable as broader diffraction peaks and reduced Debye temperatures.
The hypothesis applies to nanoparticles where atomic-scale bonding and mass differences dominate the thermal response.
